subject: Zephyr-Mini integration: request for short-term version hold + canary playbook
messages:
From: Nina Torres <nina@edgescale.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 28 Mar 2028 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Zephyr-Mini (v2.1) — tokenization differences in production samples

Hi Laura / Karthik,

We ran a subset of our integration test suite against the Zephyr-Mini v2.1 artifact you pushed last night. We're seeing ~2% tokenization divergence vs the Zephyr-Mini v2.0 baseline on our prompt set. That difference is causing subtle truncation in some autocomplete flows and one-off hallucinations where punctuation is tokenized differently.

Attached: zephyr-mini-compat-report.csv (summary), tokenizer-diff.patch (example diffs from our tokenizer shim).

Can you advise whether Redwood can pin v2.0 for EdgeScale while we investigate, or provide a quick canary window to validate v2.1 with our traffic? We prefer a short, controlled canary rather than a blanket rollback.

Thanks,
Nina Torres
Head of Integrations, EdgeScale
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Nina Torres <nina@edgescale.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 28 Mar 2028 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Zephyr-Mini (v2.1) — tokenization differences in production samples

Nina — thanks for the quick report and attachments. I've looped in Karthik (runtime/compat), Marcus (telemetry), and Marissa (onboarding/product) to scope the ask.

Short answers up front:
- We can provision a per-account temporary pin to v2.0 for EdgeScale for up to 72 hours while we run focused diagnostics.
- Alternatively, we can run a 1% traffic canary to v2.1 with additional token-level telemetry and an automatic fallback to v2.0 if mismatch/error rates exceed thresholds.

Karthik — can you confirm any immediate red flags in the compatibility report and estimate a quick turn on a per-account pin? Marcus — can you propose the telemetry metrics and thresholds for the canary (token mismatch rate, completion truncation, perplexity delta)?

I'll coordinate with EdgeScale on the choice. If they want the pin, we'll treat as a provisional hold while we validate fixes.

—Laura
Laura Bennett
Director, Product — Serving
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 28 Mar 2028 11:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Zephyr-Mini (v2.1) — tokenization differences in production samples

Quick technical read: the csv and patch show differences concentrated around byte-level normalization for quoted punctuation and some spacings in multi-byte emoji sequences. Not a model architecture regression per se — looks like the tokenizer conversion pipeline changed default normalization.

Implications:
- If we pin EdgeScale to v2.0, there is no risk to their traffic; pin is a straightforward router rule tied to the account id.
- Canary is also doable. For safety we should enable the following telemetry hooks: token-level alignment metric (tokens_in_common / tokens_total), completion-length delta, prompt+response checksum mismatch, and 5xx/error counts. Add a guard to automatically cut the canary if token alignment drops below 98.5% or completion truncation spikes >1.5x baseline.

I'll prepare a short runbook to implement the pin and the canary guard. ETA ~3 hours to have the rule and monitoring in staging, ~6 hours to roll to production (canary).

-Karthik
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 29 Mar 2028 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Zephyr-Mini (v2.1) — tokenization differences in production samples

Adding the telemetry draft and suggested thresholds (attached runbook: canary-runbook-draft.md). Summary:
- token_alignment (rolling 1h): alert if < 98.5%
- avg_completion_length (rolling 15m): alert if > baseline * 1.5
- token_truncation_errors (count/1k requests): alert if > 3
- fallback_trigger: immediate rollback to v2.0 for the affected account if any alert fires during canary window

Operational note: we should also capture a sample set of mismatched prompts to a secure S3 bucket for post-mortem (EdgeScale consent required).

Marcus
Senior SRE, Serving Runtime
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Nina Torres <nina@edgescale.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 30 Mar 2028 17:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Zephyr-Mini (v2.1) — tokenization differences in production samples

Nina — following internal validation, we can offer two safe paths:

1) Immediate per-account pin to Zephyr-Mini v2.0 for EdgeScale for up to 72 hours while we resolve tokenizer normalization. We'll create the router rule today; no schema changes or infra work for you.

2) A short, controlled canary for 1% of EdgeScale traffic to v2.1 with the monitoring/guards Marcus outlined and automatic fallback to v2.0 on alert conditions. We'll also capture anonymized mismatch samples for analysis (with your sign-off).

Please let us know which you prefer. If you take option 2 we will schedule a canary start window (day/time) and share the runbook and the Jira ticket INF-7192 that will track remediation.

Thanks — we want to minimize disruption to your users and move quickly.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Director, Product — Serving
Redwood Inference

--- Attachments referenced: zephyr-mini-compat-report.csv, tokenizer-diff.patch, canary-runbook-draft.md
